description.narrative: The Project will support the Government of Bangladesh (the government) in addressing immediate and urgent needs for financial, logistical, and systemic support to respond to the COVID-19 outbreak. The Project will support the procurement of equipment and supplies, the upgrading of health and testing facilities, and build system and community capacities for surveillance, prevention, and response to COVID-19.

description.narrative: Health and wellbeing of COVID-19 affected persons improved.

By 2023, 65% of suspected domestic COVID-19 cases reported and investigated as per MOHFW guidelines, with sex- and age disaggregated data (March 2020 baseline: 0) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. 100% of all the suspected domestic cases have been reported and investigated as per Ministry guidelines, with sex and age disaggregated data. As of 30 April 2024, the total number of investigated cases were 1,28,67,329 (Male: 94,10,011; Female: 34,55,909 and Others: 1409). Total positive cases: 17,47,425 (Male: 10,75,047; Female: 6,72,102 and Others: 276). Total negative cases: 1,11,19,904 (Male: 83,34,964; Female: 27,83,807; and Others: 1133); Data source: Management Information System of DGHS. It should be noted that no data on sample collection is received from MIS, DGHS during this reporting quarter. Data source: https://dghs-dashboard.com/pages/covid19.php. Data Source: MOHFW/ DGHS/IEDCR and PIU Actual value: Y
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Health system and community capacities in combatting COVID-19 strengthened. Indicator: By 2023, at least 200 health professionals and technical staff recruited/contracted (including at least 30% eligible women) (Baseline: 0, March 2020) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Achieved. By April 2024, 11,040 health professionals and technical staff recruited on an emergency basis to combat COVID-19 pandemic. Of them, 7,311 (66%) were women and 3,729 (34%) were men.
- Out of 2000 doctors 600 [30%] were women and 1,400 [70%]) were men; - Out of 6,000 nurses 5,700 [95%] were women and 300 [5%] were men; - Out of 386 medical technologists 135 [35%] were women and 251 [65%] men; - Out of 2,654 lab attendants 876 [33%] were women and 1,778 [67%] were men. Source: PIU. Data Source: MOHFW/DGHS and PIU Actual value: N

Output: Health system and community capacities in combatting COVID-19 strengthened. Indicator: By October 2023, at least 2 operational research completed on COVID-19 testing and case treatment. (Baseline: not in place, March 2020) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Not Achieved. Procurement was Open tender method according to procurement plan which was not practicable as no firm was available for the research. PIU proposed direct procurement method for recruitment. The time the proposal was approved and contacted to the relevant medical hospitals, they refused to conduct the research for lack of time needed for the research. Source: PIU.
Data Source: MOHFW/ IEDCR and PIU

Output: Infrastructure and related equipment for supporting and sustaining prevention and management of COVID-19 delivered. Indicator: By October 2023, at least 10 of 37 medical college hospitals equipped with intensive care units. (Baseline: 0 facilities, March 2020) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. Setting up of ICUs in 10 MCHs mentioned in output 2b were completed and are functional. Source: PIU backed by PCR survey. Data Source: MOHFW/DGHS/PWD and PIU Actual value: Y

Output: Infrastructure and related equipment for supporting and sustaining prevention and management of COVID-19 delivered. Indicator: By October 2023, at least 10 of 37 medical college hospitals equipped with isolation units. (All units have provision for segregated space for women patients) (Baseline: 0 facilities, March 2020) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. Well-equipped Isolation units were constructed and handed over that was used for treatment of COVID-19 patients. The centers were constructed in 10 public MCHs in 5 divisions. The constructed isolation centers were used for different purposes when COVID-19 was over like converting to ward, extended ICU, extended emergency service, hall room are functional Source: PIU backed by PCR survey. Data Source: MOHFW/DGHS/PWD and PIU Actual value: Y

Output: Infrastructure and related equipment for supporting and sustaining prevention and management of COVID-19 delivered. Indicator: By October 2023, at least 22 hospitals are equipped with oxygen generator plants. (Baseline: 0 facilities, March 2020) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Achieved. All 22 Oxygen Generator Plants were supplied in 22 hospitals. Source: PIU. Data Source: MOHFW/CMSD/DGHS and PIU Actual value: N

Output: Infrastructure and related equipment for supporting and sustaining prevention and management of COVID-19 delivered. Indicator: By October 2023, at least 3 of 12 points-of-entry upgraded (with separate screening booths for women) and fully functional for screening and identifying cases of COVID-19 as per MOHFW guidelines/standards. (Baseline: 0 points-of-entry, March 2020) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Not Achieved. Construction works completed for one medical center at points-of-entry at Akhaura land port. Construction of remaining 2 land ports (Tamabil and Benapole) was dropped due to unavailability of suitable land. Source: PIU. Data Source: MOHFW/MOHA/NBR/BLPA/BR/DGHS/PWD and PIU Actual value: Y

Output: Infrastructure and related equipment for supporting and sustaining prevention and management of COVID-19 delivered. Indicator: By October 2023, at least 300 staff (including 90% of all relevant women) reported increased knowledge on intensive care operation and management. Achievement: N Progress/Status: Achieved. By April 2024, 338 staff (doctors and nurses) imparted training on ICU operation and management of which 171 were female. All available relevant female staff (100%) of ICU were included in the training. Source: PIU. Data Source: MOHFW/ IEDCR and PIU Actual value: N

Output: Infrastructure and related equipment for supporting and sustaining prevention and management of COVID-19 delivered. Indicator: By October 2023, at least 40 staff (including 90% of all relevant women) reported increased knowledge on laboratory skills. Achievement: N Progress/Status: Achieved. By April 2024, 276 staff (doctors and medical technologists) imparted training on laboratory skills of which 121 were female. All available relevant female staff (100%) were included in the training. Source: PIU. Data Source: DGHS and PIU Actual value: N

Output: Infrastructure and related equipment for supporting and sustaining prevention and management of COVID-19 delivered. Indicator: By October 2023, at least 19 laboratories upgraded with COVID-19 microbiological diagnostic facilities with testing capacity of 180 per day per facility, as per MOHFW guidelines (Baseline: 16 laboratories for testing but not upgraded, March 2020) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. By April 2024, total 19 laboratories were upgraded or constructed with a capacity of 345 tests per day per facility totaling 6,555 tests per day. Source: PIU. Data Source: MOHFW/IEDCR and PIU Actual value: Y

Output: Health system and community capacities in combatting COVID-19 strengthened. Indicator: By October 2023, inclusive and gender responsive COVID-19 risk communication strategy and plan reviewed and disseminated among the relevant stakeholders. Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. By October 2023, inclusive and gender responsive COVID-19 risk communication strategy and plan reviewed in November 2023 and disseminated 29 2024 at IPH (Institute of Public Health among the relevant stakeholders (DGHS, DGFP, MOH&FW, NGOs, DPs). Source: PIU. Data Source: MOHFW/ DGHS and PIU Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2023 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Immediate and medium-term equipment needs for testing and managing COVID-19 met. Indicator: By May 2023, emergency equipment and personal protective equipment for men and women for managing COVID-19 outbreak procured and distributed to national and district health facilities (March 2020 baseline: 0). Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. By April 2024, total 20 packages were contracted (9 by PIU and 11 by CMSD consisting of emergency equipment and PPE respectively. Of them, procurement of 19 packages completed (9 for PIU, and 10 for CMSD). Procurement of 1 contract for 8 oxygen generator plants could not be completed for failure from supplier side in due time (on or before 30 April 2024). Emergency equipment was distributed to 10 MCHs and PPEs were distributed to 2,300,000 health workers and emergency response team workers in national and district-level health facilities (1,380,000 women (60%). Source: PIU and CMSD. Data Source: MOHFW/ DGHS and PIU Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
